chunks: With this chain of transmission, from Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from ʿAli ibn al-Hakam, from Aban, from Abi Usamah and Abi Yusuf Yaʿqub ibn ʿUthaym, from Abi ʿAbd Allah عليه السلام, who said:

If a bird, a chicken, or a mouse falls into the well, then draw seven buckets from it. We said: What do you say regarding our salat (prayer), our wudu (ablution), and what has touched our clothes? He said: There is no harm in it.

key_terms.الدَّجَاجَةُ: a chicken falling into the well
key_terms.الطَّيْرُ: a bird falling into the well
key_terms.الْبِئْرِ: the well from which water is drawn
key_terms.الْفَأْرَةُ: a mouse falling into the well
key_terms.سَبْعَ دِلَاءٍ: seven buckets to be drawn from the well
key_terms.صَلَاتِنَا: our salat (prayer) performed using or after contact with that water
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: there is no harm in it; no problem is established
key_terms.وُضُوئِنَا: our wudu (ablution) done with that water

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a bird, chicken, or mouse falls into a well, and does it affect salat (prayer), wudu (ablution), or clothing?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding a well into which certain animals have fallen. It instructs that seven buckets be drawn from the well, while affirming that salat (prayer), wudu (ablution), and clothes affected by that water are not invalidated or harmed.
